answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a scarce token in a public stake contract before it can submit jobs or earn fees. The contract releases the stake only after a challenge window, during which peers can prove duplicated control by signing a fresh, unpredictable kernel challenge with the same key. A confirmed duplicate forfeits the stake to reporters. Creating a fake ocean of identities therefore requires capital for each one, and detected Sybils lose that capital; the river of fees rewards useful agents, not names alone.
